messages:
olivia: Escalation from customer INC-4321 — their production app started failing validation after yesterday's model update. They report pydantic ValidationError: value is not a valid enumeration member. Here's the model output we captured in JSON mode.

support-bot: Attached transcript and ticket link: https://redwood.ai/ticket/INC-4321

kevin: Can you paste the actual response bytes? Could be number vs string or stray punctuation.

olivia: Sure, raw snippet we logged from the stream:
```
{"user_id": "1234", "status": 1, "details": {"reason":"ok"}}
```
Previously status was "active"/"inactive" strings. Our jsonschema expects enum ["active","inactive"]. Pydantic raises:
```
pydantic.error_wrappers.ValidationError: 1 validation error for Response
status
  value is not a valid enumeration member; permitted: 'active', 'inactive' (type=type_error.enum; enum_values=['active','inactive'])
```
alejandro: Sounds like the model started emitting ordinal values for enums. Could be a change in the prompt or an upstream finetune. Which model/version are they on?

olivia: Hosted call used model "redwood-ggml-v1.4" pinned to v2026-03-14. Customer says they didn't change anything client-side. They use JSONMODE with strict pydantic validation. Also saw intermittent trailing comma in arrays when streaming, e.g., ["flag1",].

kevin: Repro checklist: 1) raw request you used 2) prompt template 3) schema. Can you paste them?

olivia: Repro payload we sent:
```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
{
  "model": "redwood-ggml-v1.4",
  "json_mode": true,
  "prompt": "Return user account state as JSON. Fields: user_id, status (active/inactive), flags (array of strings).",
  "temperature": 0.0
}
```

Schema snippet:
```
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "user_id": {"type":"string"},
    "status":{"type":"string","enum":["active","inactive"]},
    "flags":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}}
  },
  "required":["user_id","status"]
}
```

sre-oncall: I'm seeing increased 5xxs for redwood-ggml-v1.4 starting 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC. Could be a rollout. kevin / alejandro, any changes that would cause enum tokens to be emitted as numbers?

kevin: Not intentionally. Two quick hypotheses: 1) tokenizer/decoder change in the model build causing label tokens to map differently, 2) prompt examples in the new artifact included numeric labels (e.g., "status: 1"). Will inspect the artifact diff.

alejandro: I'll pull generation traces and few-shot contexts. In the meantime, recommend the customer add a small tolerant normalizer that coerces ints -> strings for enum fields and strips trailing commas as a short-term workaround.

olivia: Customer is on Dedicated plan and wants an ETA. Marked INC-4321 P1 and cc'd eng.

kevin: I'll spin up the internal test harness and try to reproduce with strict pydantic and zod. If it's model-side, we'll either rollback or pin the previous artifact for them. Will report back by EOD.

support-bot: Incident created: INC-4321 | priority:P1 | assignees: kevin, alejandro

olivia: Also, add note that one customer reported streaming JSON occasionally contained a trailing comma in arrays (e.g., ["flag1",]) which breaks strict parsers. Include that in repro.

kevin: Got it. I'll run strict parse tests for both pydantic (python) and zod (node) and open a regression test if we can reproduce.

alejandro: Quick update — found a diff in the model artifact: v2026-03-14 changed the internal prompt template; an example in the prompt used numeric labels for status. Rolling back that prompt change in canary now.

sre-oncall: Canary rollback initiated. Monitoring error and latency metrics.

olivia: Updating the customer that we rolled back the prompt patch and are monitoring. They'll test and confirm. Thanks everyone. :)
